messages:
marta: Quick heads-up — I ran a cross-cloud sweep (AWS/GCP/Azure) against the same A100 SKU and CUDA stack matrix. Used our interleaved load pattern (mixed small+long seqs) to surface scheduling regressions. Azure is showing consistent p95 spikes while AWS/GCP look steady. Dumping summary and snippets below.

hao: Nice, can you paste the harness command + driver versions?

marta: Sure — harness: ```./bench-run --model red-3b --seq 1024 --batch 8 --pattern interleaved --samples 10 --quant int8 --warmup 200```\nDrivers: AWS/GCP: 525.85, Azure: 520.61 (both CUDA 12.1 builds). Also tried pinned repro with kernel 6.1 vs 6.5 on Azure nodes.

samir: Are the Azure machines the same machine type (v4/v3) or different underlying firmware? sometimes frequency governor/IRQ affinity differs.

marta: Same SKU (A100 80GB) family across providers but Azure VMs had different BIOS microcode and older driver. Also noticed more nv_peer_memory / NVLINK init logs on Azure at boot.

maya: Any perf numbers? p50/p95/p99?

marta: Quick paste: ```
# AWS (525.85)
p50: 42ms
p95: 58ms
p99: 88ms
throughput: 320 toks/sec
# GCP (525.85)
p50: 40ms
p95: 60ms
p99: 89ms
throughput: 325 toks/sec
# Azure (520.61)
p50: 45ms
p95: 210ms    <-- big tail
p99: 480ms
throughput: 295 toks/sec
```

marta: Note: when running single-stream (non-interleaved) Azure p95 matches others. So it's specifically the interleaved pattern / scheduling. Also int8 quant runs on Azure showed lower throughput compared to fp16 (unexpected).

hao: That smells like a kernel scheduler or pinned-thread/CUDA context switch issue under mixed seq workloads. Can you grab dmesg / nvidia-smi --query and `top -H` during a spike?

marta: Pasted snippets: ```
# during spike (Azure)
[  +0.001234] NVRM: GPU at pci:0000:3d:00: Unable to schedule work, falling back
# nvidia-smi sampled during spike
GPU Util: 20%, Memory Util: 45%, NVLink errors: 0
# top -H shows host threads stalling in futex_wait
```

samir: Futex stalls indicate user-space lock contention. Our interleaved harness uses a small thread pool per inference worker and a shared KV cache mutex. Could be a contention hotspot exposed by Azure kernel's futex implementation or different glibc build.

marta: Good call. I ran an instrumented build that records lock hold times. Median hold <1ms, but 0.1% of locks held for 120-300ms on Azure only.

maya: That would explain p95/p99. Any differences in scheduler params? e.g., CONFIG_PREEMPT, or cpuset affinity in our VM images?

marta: Azure images had the azure-custom kernel config (preempt=voluntary) vs AWS/GCP images preempt=full. Also irqbalance service disabled by default on Azure which changed CPU isolation.

hao: Two-pronged repro plan: 1) run with preempt=full kernel (if possible) or tune futex_priority inheritance; 2) remove the shared KV mutex by switching to sharded caches to see if contention disappears.

marta: Ran quick sharded cache build (4 shards) — spikes vanish on Azure p95 back to ~62ms. Throughput also recovers to ~320 toks/sec. So it's indeed lock contention exacerbated by Azure kernel+image defaults.

samir: Great find. Can you also try with the newer 525.x Azure driver? maybe driver 520.x had a user-space wait path that interacts poorly with kernel futex (we saw similar once with cublas fallback).

marta: Will try. One more oddity: int8 quant throughput drop on Azure traced to small GEMM paths using cuBLASLt falling back to do small-K GEMMs in FP32 due to missing optimized kernels in 520.x. Dumped cuBLAS logs show fallback path triggered for MxK shapes ~64x128.

marta: cuBLAS log snippet: ```
CUBLASLT: chosen algo=FALLBACK_FP32 for op=bmm_int8 M=64 K=128 N=512
```

maya: So two independent contributors: (1) lock contention + kernel config causing tail latency; (2) driver/cuBLAS kernel availability causing int8 throughput regression. Both plausible.

hao: Action items: 1) marta -> run same interleaved harness on Azure with 525.85 driver and preempt=full kernel (or new image) and paste p95 numbers. 2) samir -> draft short doc on sharded-KV change to avoid mutex. 3) infra -> evaluate standardizing kernel preempt settings for inference images. 4) maya -> open driver bug with vendor referencing cuBLASLt fallback.

marta: I opened an internal bug: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4321 (contains logs + minimal repro harness). Will run driver upgrade next.

dev-bot: Test artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/1899991111/artifacts.tar.gz

marta: TL;DR for oncall/bring-up: if you see p95 tails on interleaved load on Azure A100 SKU, first try sharded cache (workaround) and verify driver >=525.85 and kernel preempt=full. I'll post results after the driver run. :white_check_mark:
